# Small additions to arbitrary simplex parity cores

This is a scoped auxiliary theorem. It does not show that an arbitrary
mixed-integer source has the required concentration on a parity core.

For every d>=2 there is rho_d>0 with the following property, independently
of n>=1. Let C subset R^n times R^d be a compact convex body. Suppose
P0 subset Z^n contains exactly one representative of each class modulo
2Z^n, and the actual fibers K_w=C_w, w in P0, are d-simplices of the
same positive volume V. They may have different shapes, orientations,
and positions. Put N=2^n and

    E=sum_(p outside P0) vol_d(C_p).

If E<=rho_d V, then an actual point in a core fiber has every containing
closed ambient halfspace of mass at least

    (Gamma_d/N)(NV+E).                                  (1)

No convex-position, empty-polytope, cube, common-shape, or common-centroid
assumption on P0 or its fibers is imposed. The proof uses ordinary
continuous Grunbaum and its simplex equality case, and proves its
additional finite-dimensional lemmas below.

## 1. The parity shell and disjoint endpoint pairs

For any nonempty outside fiber A_p=C_p, let v(p) in P0 have the same
parity as p and put w(p)=(p+v(p))/2. Convexity puts this integer point
in the projection of C. For any a in A_p its fiber contains
(a+K_v)/2 and hence has volume at least 2^-d V.

Consequently E<2^-d V implies w(p) in P0. Every nonempty outside
fiber, including a zero-volume one, then has base p=2w-v for two
different core points. This is a finite set of at most N(N-1) bases.
For a fixed w the corresponding partners v=2w-p are all distinct
and none equals w. Thus endpoint-pair contributions can be summed
without reusing the middle fiber or any partner fiber.

Group the positive outside fibers by w, writing E_w for their total
mass. Then sum_w E_w=E, so some w has E_w>=E/N. We shall prove a
local bound

    all caps at one point of K_w have mass
       >=Gamma_d V+Gamma_d E_w,                        (2)

for every w with E_w>0. This implies (1). If E=0 the ordinary
centroid of any core fiber suffices.

## 2. A determinant bound giving many facet credits

Write m=d+1, b=1/m, J=ceil(m/2), L=m-J+1, and

    Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d,
    delta=m^(-m/(2L))-1/m>0,
    kappa=J/m-Gamma>0.                                 (3)

Positivity of delta follows from m/(2L)<1, and kappa>0 follows
from J/m>=1/2>Gamma for d>=2.

Let T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), of volume V0=1/d!, with barycentric
functions lambda_0,...,lambda_d. If B is any simplex of volume V0
and (a+B)/2 subset T, write its d+1 transformed vertices in
barycentric columns of T, obtaining a nonnegative column-stochastic
m by m matrix P with

    |det P|=2^-d.

Let p_1>=...>=p_m be its row maxima. Replace the row having maximum
p_1 by the sum of all rows, which is the all-one row. This preserves
the determinant up to a sign from reordering. From every other row
subtract its maximum divided by two times this all-one row. Every
entry then has absolute value at most p_i/2. Hadamard's determinant
bound gives

    |det P|<=m^(m/2) 2^(-(m-1)) product_(i=2)^m p_i
             <=m^(m/2) 2^(-(m-1)) p_J^L.

The last inequality uses p_i<=1 for i<J and p_i<=p_J for i>=J.
Therefore at least J rows have maximum at least b+delta.
Equivalently, at least J indices i satisfy

    lambda_i(a)+max_B lambda_i >= 2b+2delta.            (4)

This conclusion concerns each a individually; the good indices may
vary with a. No common choice is presumed.

## 3. Fixed endpoint credits, with translation-invariant perturbation bounds

Fix one core point w with E_w>0 and apply ONE invertible affine map
of all continuous coordinates sending K_w to T. It preserves every
integer base and every ambient halfspace and multiplies all d-masses
by the same factor; hence all ratios E/V and E_w/V are unchanged.
The partner fibers B_p=K_(v(p)) are still simplices of volume V0,
and the actual compatibility inclusion is

    (A_p+B_p)/2 subset T.                              (5)

Define measurable fixed credit sets

    A_(p,i)={a in A_p:lambda_i(a)+max_(B_p)lambda_i
                              >=2b+delta},
    c_i=sum_p vol_d(A_(p,i)),    cbar=(1/m)sum_i c_i.

Equation (4), integrated over each A_p, proves

    0<=c_i<=E_w,       cbar>=J E_w/m.                  (6)

All sums in this section use only the group belonging to w. Let
f=lambda_i+e dot x with |e|<=epsilon, and let y in T satisfy
max_i(lambda_i(y)-b)_+<=sigma. Put r_p=(|A_p|/V0)^(1/d).

For every a in A_(p,i), (5) implies a+B_p subset 2T. Since T is
contained in the Euclidean unit ball, perturbing its SUM support
functional gives

    f(a)+max_(B_p) f >=2b+delta-2epsilon.               (7)

This bound does not require either A_p or B_p to lie in a common
ball about zero: their translations cancel in a+B_p. Likewise

    f(y)<=b+sigma+epsilon,
    width_(B_p)(f)<=2 width_T(f)<=2+4epsilon.            (8)

Therefore

    f(a)+max_(B_p)f-2f(y)-width_(B_p)(f) r_p
       >=delta-2sigma-4epsilon-(2+4epsilon)r_p.         (9)

Choose epsilon<=min{delta/32,1/4}, sigma<=delta/8 and
r_p<=delta/16. The right side is strictly positive.

Here is why this is a uniform cap credit. In a closed ambient cap
whose boundary passes through (w,y), the two thresholds for the
opposite bases p and v=2w-p sum to 2f(y). A homothetic copy of B_p
toward an f-maximizer with ratio r_p lies in the cap at threshold
max_(B_p)f-width_(B_p)(f)r_p and has volume |A_p|. If the actual
B_p cap has at least this much mass, it pays the entire credit.
Otherwise its threshold is strictly larger than that displayed
threshold, so the actual A_p threshold is strictly smaller than
2f(y)-max_(B_p)f+width_(B_p)(f)r_p. Equations (7)--(9) then put
ALL of A_(p,i) strictly inside the A_p cap. Thus in either case
the endpoint pair contributes at least |A_(p,i)|, for every real
integer tilt. Summing disjoint pairs gives at least c_i.

## 4. A small translation of the actual simplex centroid

Let g be the centroid of T and n_i=grad lambda_i. Put

    eta=kappa/2,       Kd=sqrt(d)/(m Gamma).

There is a unique vector v with

    n_i dot v=(c_i-cbar)/(m Gamma V0),   i=0,...,d.       (10)

Indeed the right sides sum to zero and the barycentric gradients
have that sole dependence. Set y=g+v. Equations (6) and (10) give

    |v|<=Kd E_w/V0,
    max_i(lambda_i(y)-b)_+<=E_w/(m Gamma V0).            (11)

In particular y is in int T for sufficiently small E/V, uniformly
in w and the shapes of all its partners.

We record the elementary local derivative estimate used to balance
the credits. For each i and f=lambda_i+e dot x, with e small, the
vertex at which lambda_i=1 remains the unique vertex above every
level f(g)+t with |t| small. The cap is then a simplex and its volume
has the exact formula

    V0 [f(v_i)-f(g)-t]^d /
                 product_(j not i)[f(v_i)-f(v_j)].      (12)

Its positive coarea density is the negative derivative in t. At
e=0,t=0 this density equals m Gamma V0. All denominators remain
strictly positive near this point. By continuity of the finitely
many displayed rational functions, for every zeta>0 there exist
epsilon_0,h>0, depending only on d and zeta, such that for all i,
|e|<=epsilon_0 and |t|<=h the density differs from m Gamma V0 by
at most zeta V0. Formula (12) proves this without any boundary
smoothness assumption.

Choose zeta>0 and then epsilon>0 small enough that, in addition
to Section 3 and this density estimate,

    zeta (sqrt(d)+1) Kd<=eta/2,
    sqrt(d) epsilon<=eta/2.                            (13)

If E/V is also small enough to make
|f(y)-f(g)|<h, the signed coarea integral, (10), (11) and (13) give

    | mass_T{f>=f(y)}-mass_T{f>=f(g)}
                   +m Gamma V0 n_i dot v |<=eta E_w.   (14)

Ordinary Grunbaum at the TRUE centroid g makes the initial cap
mass at least Gamma V0. Adding the endpoint credit from Section 3
to (14) proves, for every such near-facet direction and every tilt,

    total cap mass >=Gamma V0+cbar-eta E_w
                    >=Gamma V0+(Gamma+kappa/2)E_w.     (15)

## 5. Remaining directions, a uniform constant, and closed boundary mass

Put theta_i=n_i/|n_i| and rho=epsilon/sqrt(d). Every unit normal
u with |u-theta_i|<=rho is covered by Section 4 after multiplying
its full halfspace inequality by |n_i|>0. This multiplication also
rescales its unrestricted integer normal, and makes no restriction
on oblique orientations.

For the standard simplex at its centroid, the continuous Grunbaum
minimum Gamma occurs exactly at theta_0,...,theta_d. Its normalized
cap function F is continuous on the unit sphere. Hence on the
compact complement of these open rho-neighborhoods it has a positive
gap G above Gamma. If that complement is empty, omit the following
gap restrictions. A cap movement of distance |v| changes its mass
inside T by at most kappa_(d-1)|v|, since T lies in the unit ball.
Thus for sufficiently small E/V all remaining directions receive
at least Gamma V0+(G/2)V0 from the middle fiber alone, which exceeds
Gamma V0+Gamma E_w after decreasing the same bound on E/V if needed.

All the smallness requirements above can be met by ONE rho_d>0:
first choose delta,kappa,eta,zeta,epsilon,h in the stated order;
then choose rho_d so that

    rho_d<2^-d,
    rho_d<min{1,Gamma/4,m Gamma delta/8,(delta/16)^d},
    (sqrt(d)+1)Kd rho_d<h,
    [kappa_(d-1)Kd/V0]rho_d<G/2,
    Gamma rho_d<G/2.

The last two requirements are omitted if there is no complementary
direction set. Every quantity depends only on d and is strictly
positive. In particular (11) ensures y in int T, sigma<=delta/8,
and every r_p<=delta/16. The inequalities may all be made strict
while allowing the hypothesis E<=rho_d V by selecting a smaller
positive rho_d once at the end.

A through-center cap with zero continuous normal contains the
ENTIRE core fiber, with its boundary mass, and therefore has mass
at least V. Since N>=2, Gamma<1/2 and rho_d<1, this exceeds
Gamma(V+E/N). Every containing closed halfspace includes its
parallel halfspace whose boundary passes through the chosen point.
The near-facet estimate (15), the complementary-direction estimate,
and the zero-normal case therefore prove (1) for every closed
ambient halfspace. Nonvertical boundaries are d-volume null inside
each fiber, but no such nullness was assumed for vertical caps.

Finally choose w with E_w>=E/N and undo its ONE continuous affine
normalization. The point remains a single deterministic point of
the original core fiber; the common Jacobian cancels from (1).
There are finitely many nonempty fibers, their H_d masses add, and
the positive core fibers give q=d and positive finite total mass.
Zero-volume outside fibers were included in the parity-shell step
and are harmless in the mass sum. This completes the scoped proof.

The case n=0 has only one integer fiber and follows from continuous
Grunbaum. The d=1 OC bound follows from the ordinary mixed Helly
bound 1/2^(n+1); the positive facet-credit margin used here is not
claimed in that case. No new treatment of arbitrary lower-dimensional
intrinsic fibers or d=0 is supplied by this auxiliary theorem.
